text: And this beacon is indeed a way to provide time reference for all the other nodes of the network, so that they can be considered as synchronized. If the coordinator does that, then we say that our network works in beacon enabled mode. Okay. So let's first look indeed at this case where we have beacons that are periodically transmitted by the coordinator. And it's easier to understand what is the organization of the node's activity in the network by looking at this picture. So as I said in this case, when the beacon is enabled, we have super frames. The super frame is again the time between two subsequent beacons, like in Wi-Fi. And then within a super frame, we have two phases. One in which we use the contention based access, and the other one in which we use the contention free access. So very similar to what we had again in Wi-Fi. But the the two are swapped, so we have this contention based access first, and then the contention free period afterwards. Now if we look into each of these phases, we can see here.
